scenes.title: Data Contracts
scenes.subtitle: Agreements between producers and consumers
scenes.narration: A data contract is an explicit, enforceable agreement about the schema, semantics, and quality of the data a producer supplies to consumers.

scenes.heading: What a contract specifies
bullets: Semantics: what each field actually means
Ownership and a process for changes
scenes.narration: A contract pins down the schema so consumers know exactly what shape to expect. It also captures semantics, clarifying what each field means to prevent misuse. Crucially it states quality guarantees like freshness and completeness, and it names an owner along with a defined process for making changes.

scenes.heading: How contracts are enforced
steps: Producer publishes the contract as code
CI validates changes against the contract
Data is checked against it at runtime
Breaking changes are versioned and negotiated
scenes.narration: The producer publishes the contract as version-controlled code so it becomes the single source of truth. Continuous integration then validates any producer change against the contract before it ships. At runtime the flowing data is checked against the same contract, and breaking changes must be explicitly versioned and negotiated with consumers.

scenes.heading: A data contract in YAML
scenes.code:
contract: orders
owner: checkout-team
schema:
  - name: order_id
    type: string
    nullable: false
    unique: true
  - name: amount
    type: decimal
    nullable: false
    constraints: { min: 0 }
sla:
  freshness: 1h
  completeness: 0.99
version: 2.0.0
scenes.narration: This contract names the orders dataset and assigns clear ownership to the checkout team. The schema block declares each field's type, nullability, and constraints, including a non-negative amount. The SLA block encodes quality guarantees for freshness and completeness, and the semantic version signals compatibility to every consumer.

scenes.text: A contract turns implicit assumptions into an enforced, versioned agreement that prevents surprise breakages.
scenes.narration: By writing expectations as code and checking them in CI and at runtime, contracts shift quality upstream to the producer. Versioning makes breaking changes a deliberate, negotiated event instead of an outage.
